branding.title: AGIL® Secure Identity
branding.subtitle:
Biometric enrolment, passenger clearance and access
for airports, checkpoints and secure sites

products.name: Enrolment Kiosk
products.description: Self-service biometric enrolment: scan an ID, capture a live face, and issue a pass in one visit.

features.title: Face Cameras
features.description: A colour camera and an infrared camera work as a pair. Together they capture a quality-checked face photo and confirm that a live person is present, not a printed photo or a screen. Infrared illumination keeps capture consistent in bright lobbies and dim corridors alike.

features.title: Touchscreen
features.description: A 13.3-inch portrait touchscreen walks each person through enrolment one step at a time, with on-screen and spoken prompts. A reach mode moves every control to the lower part of the screen for wheelchair users.

features.title: QR Scanner
features.description: Reads a QR code straight from a phone screen or a printed letter, so a pre-registered person is recognised immediately and only has to confirm their details.

features.title: Passport & ID Reader
features.description: Place a passport or ID card face-down on the glass. The reader captures the full page, reads the printed text, and reads the electronic chip in an ePassport. The chip photo is then compared with the live face, tying the document to the person holding it.

features.title: Pass Printer
features.description:
Prints and cuts a pass or receipt as soon as enrolment is complete. The printer sits on a slide-out drawer, so paper can be changed from the front in under a minute.

A mobile pass can be issued instead of paper.

features.title: Status Light
features.description: A light bar across the top shows the kiosk's state from across the room: ready, in use, done, or needs attention. A presence sensor wakes the kiosk as someone approaches.

features.title: Fits Any Site
features.description: One core unit mounts on a desk, wall or floor stand and runs from a single network cable that also carries power. The device starts only trusted software, encrypts its storage, and keeps no personal data once a record has been sent to the back-end system.

features.title: Where It's Used
features.description: Airports: enrol staff, contractors and travellers once, so later checkpoints only need a face. Police: register visitors and verify identity at the front counter without tying up an officer. Defence: enrol visitors and contractors at the camp gate before a pass is issued.

products.name: APICS
products.description: Self-service passenger clearance: document, face, iris and fingerprint checked at one kiosk.

features.title: Face & Iris Cameras
features.description: The camera bar captures the traveller's face and, using near-infrared light, the unique pattern of each iris. Near-infrared makes iris detail visible regardless of eye colour or ambient lighting, and both captures are quality-checked before they are accepted.

features.title: Guided Screen
features.description: Clear, step-by-step prompts tell the traveller where to look and what to present, so first-time users clear without help from an officer.

features.title: Passport Reader
features.description: Reads the passport data page and the electronic chip, and checks the document's security features. The chip photo becomes the reference the live face is matched against.

features.title: Fingerprint Scanner
features.description: A second biometric for travellers whose face or iris cannot be matched, and for clearance rules that require fingerprints.

features.title: Status Light
features.description: Shows the traveller when to step up and when they are cleared, and shows supervising officers at a glance which kiosk needs assistance.

features.title: Where It's Used
features.description: Airports and checkpoints: automated arrival and departure clearance that keeps queues moving while officers focus on the cases that need them. Police and border agencies: consistent identity checks against watchlists at every lane. Defence: controlled entry of personnel and visitors at base checkpoints.

products.name: Nova Readers
products.description: Modular door access readers: Nova for card and PIN, Nova Plus for multi-biometric access.

features.title: Iris Recognition
features.description: Nova Plus. The iris module at the top reads the unique pattern of each iris under near-infrared light. It is contactless and gives the highest assurance of the reader's biometric modes.

features.title: Face Recognition
features.description: Nova Plus. Twin cameras verify a face hands-free as the person walks up, with a liveness check so a photo or a screen is not accepted.

features.title: QR Code
features.description: Nova Plus. A scan window beside the cameras reads QR passes from a phone or a printed slip, for visitors and temporary access.

features.title: Touchscreen
features.description: Nova Plus. Short on-screen guidance (come closer, look up, hold still) and a clear welcome when the door unlocks.

features.title: Card Tap
features.description: Nova and Nova Plus. Tap a contactless access card on the card zone. Use it alone, or pair it with a PIN or a biometric for doors that need two factors.

features.title: Fingerprint
features.description: Nova Plus. The sensor on the base matches a fingerprint by touch. It also serves as the fallback when a face or iris cannot be read, so an authorised person is not left at the door.

features.title: PIN Keypad
features.description: Nova. A touch keypad for PIN entry, used with a card for controlled doors such as control rooms and server rooms.

features.title: Where It's Used
features.description: Airports: staff access doors and identity confirmation before security screening. Police: restricted rooms such as armouries and evidence stores. Defence: secure zones and airlock doors where a card alone is not enough.
